newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez-Lyonnaise aims at 56 ffr eps in 2002 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Suez-Lyonnaise aims at 56 ffr eps in 2002 - paper.

text.p: Suez-Lyonnaise, the company to be formed by the merger of Cie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux aims to double its earnings per share to 56 francs in the year 2002, chief executive Gerard Mestrallet said in an interview with the Le Journal des Finances weekly to appear on Saturday.
"Our objective is to double the profit per share between now and 2002 to bring it to 56 francs," Mestrallet said.
He said that in 2001 the group would have sales of 180 billion francs against 102 billion in 1996.
Of the sales, more than half would be generated outside France and Belgium, he said.

"The consolidated sales figure will double in energy, it will double abroad in water, it will double in waste management and in communications it will be brought to 10 billion francs (from two billion)," he said.
He said the group was expecting a 500 million franc charge for property in 1997, based on a further 10 percent decline in the real estate market.
But this would be offset by asset gains on the sale of shares in Saint-Gobain, Factofrance and Accor .
Mestrallet said that discussions were under way with the French Treasury about whether Suez could keep its 2.5 billion francs in tax credits.
He added that asset gains by the group's Belgian unit Societe Generale de Belgique were tax free and noted that in the first year the new group would have hardly any taxable revenues in France.
He said that cooperation between Lyonnaise and Tractebel In Belgium would be mainly in foreign markets.
"Decisions will have to be taken in the interest of both companies. There will be no synergy unless both companies gain," Mestrallet said.
